Alex — thanks for the packet and quick turnaround. High level: the business is fine with most of this but legal flagged two immediate concerns.

On Output title: our counsel is uncomfortable with any language that could be read to give Redwood rights in our customers' downstream product titles or attributions. On Retraining / Feedback: we cannot accept a broad perpetual license over customer content for model training. Acceptable options from our side:
- explicit opt-in for any retrain that includes Cobalt data (Customer must sign off on dataset + usage), OR
- a time-limited telemetry license (e.g., 12 months) with anonymization and an express prohibition on using PII.

Jordan / Alex — Legal reviewed and prepared two clean alternatives. Summary and recommended compromise below; tracked redlines attached.

Summary of the position we can accept today (compromise):
- Output ownership: insert clause "Customer retains all right, title and interest in Output (meaning content generated by Customer via the Service), excluding aggregated, de-identified telemetry and service logs." This is explicit and preserves Customer title while allowing Redwood to use telemetry.

- Retrain / Feedback license (two Order Form options):
  Option A — Opt-in Retrain: "Customer may elect to grant Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, royalty-free, worldwide license to use specified Customer datasets for model training, provided Customer executes a separate written consent specifying the dataset and purpose (DocuSign or equivalent)."

  Option B — Time-limited Telemetry License: "Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, royalty-free, worldwide license to use aggregated and anonymized telemetry and feedback for model improvement for a period of twelve (12) months from the date of collection. Redwood will not use raw customer content or PII for training; all telemetry used for training will be subjected to automated de-identification procedures and logged in the customer's audit trail."

Rationale: Option A covers customers who necessitate affirmative consent for training (enterprise/regulated). Option B keeps product velocity for standard customers while giving a limited window and stronger anonymization guarantees. Both options exclude transfer of Output title to Redwood.

Action items / next steps:
- We attached redline_MSA_2026_v2.docx with both Option A and Option B inserted as alternative paragraphs in §7.2. (attachment: redline_MSA_2026_v2.docx)
- Alex / Sales: pick one option per Order Form. We recommend Option B for standard Product-tier Order Forms and Option A for Dedicated/Private deployments where customers will likely require explicit consent.
- Legal: prepare a short customer-facing FAQ snippet for the Order Form so procurement/legal at Cobalt sees the tradeoffs.

Jordan — if that looks acceptable we can send a tracked version back to Cobalt Legal now and call out which Option we're proposing for the current Order Form. Happy to hop on a 20-min call if your team wants to walk through the redlines.
